checks.what: British Africa gains Southern Rhodesia from the Company, September 1923. Page: 'the territory was annexed by the United Kingdom on 12 September 1923' and 'on 1 October 1923, the first constitution for the colony came into force'; infobox 'Self-governing British colony (1923-1965)'. The region is the Company's own 1923 loss region and resolves to 1,304 cells, exactly the cells of modern Zimbabwe (the colony's borders); the page gives 372,518 km2, and the grid gives 329,782 km2 for Zimbabwe itself. Trial replay: Zimbabwe is BSAC land in 1920-1922 and British Africa in 1923-1925 (in the published draft it is nobody's in 1923-1925). From 1926 the state is the same as the published draft and the p1930 end anchor is unchanged for Rhodesia.

British Africa gains Northern Rhodesia from the Company, April 1924. Page: 'On 1 April 1924, Herbert Stanley was appointed as Governor' and 'Northern Rhodesia became an official Protectorate of the United Kingdom', with its 'administrative machinery taken over by the Colonial Office'; area 751,925 km2. The region is the Company's own 1924 loss region and resolves to 2,528 cells: all 2,501 Zambian cells plus 27 Chobe cells in Botswana, which the Company held in the draft since its 1899 Lozi gain. That strip goes to British Africa, which is also right for Bechuanaland, so the excess does no harm. Trial replay: Zambia is BSAC land in 1923 and British Africa in 1924-1925; the 1926 state and the end anchor are unchanged.

Senussi Order gains the Kufra district from British Africa, 1/1920. Page: under al-Rajma (1920) Idris was 'permitted to administer autonomously the oases around Kufra'; Kufra was 'the last stronghold of the Senussi in Libya'; 'In 1931, Italian forces seized Kufra'. The page gives Britain no land in Libya. The counterpart british-africa is a mechanical fix: Britain held the cells only because of a Cliopatria shape. The note says so honestly. The Senussi held Kufra from 1894 (dossier ledger 4), so January 1920, the window's first month, is the right repair date. The region (Al Kufrah, 1,404 cells) lies wholly inside the Senussi 1924 and 1926 keyframes. Trial: 1,389 cells are Senussi from 1920; the 15 French (Chad-border) cells are untouched.

first-hellenic-republic_1922 (valid 1922-1923): the Cliopatria 1922 shape minus Eastern Thrace (as the dossier already had) and minus Izmir province. Page: 'The Turkish cavalry rode into the town around eleven o'clock on the Saturday morning of 9 September' and 'The expulsion of the Greek Army from Anatolia was completed on 18 September'; it gives no Greek foothold after that. The cut removes exactly the 14 Izmir cells of the 1922 shape (454 -> 390 cells against 404 before) and nothing else. Trial: those 14 cells are nobody's at the end of 1922 and Republic of Turkey's from 1923. In the published draft they were direct Greek land through 1929, after ottoman-empire/ledger/236 (contest_end) made them direct. The Greece/Turkey conflict falls from 54 to 12 cell-years (4 edge cells a year).

kingdom-of-lithuania_1924 (valid 1924-1935) minus a 47 km disc round Vilnius. Page: Central Lithuania 'was incorporated into Poland on 18 April 1922', 'Lithuania declined to accept the Polish authority', and 'Vilnius and its surroundings ... were given to Lithuania in accordance with the Soviet-Lithuanian Mutual Assistance Treaty of 10 October 1939'. The disc (30 cells) is the dossier's own Vilnius spec, the same one used in its 1920 and 1939 events and its 1939 keyframe. The cut removes exactly the 14 disc cells of the 1924 shape (290 -> 276). Trial: all 30 disc cells are Polish 1922-1929, where the published draft gave 14 of them to Lithuania from 1924. A residual 1924 conflict of 12 cells inside the 100 km disc of Poland's 1922 gain is edge noise along the demarcation line, which the entry does not touch.

second-polish-republic_1924 (valid 1924-1935) plus the same 47 km Vilnius disc. The page dates Polish rule from 18 April 1922 to October 1939. The union adds exactly the 14 disc cells the Cliopatria shape lacks (1,601 -> 1,615) and nothing else. Without this pair entry the 1924 Polish snap would drop the cells again. Trial confirms that Vilnius stays Polish to 1929.

british-africa vs senussi-order, 1920-1930, Al Kufrah (1,404 cells), winner Senussi. Page as for events/2: Kufra was Senussi until 'In 1931, Italian forces seized Kufra', so the end year 1930 is right. Trial: the ruling settles 1,389 cells in each of 1922, 1926 and 1927 (4,167 cell-years), the British Africa keyframe years, and the p1930 end anchor moves those 1,389 cells from british-africa to senussi-order. The why's quote 'last stronghold in Libya' is a close paraphrase of the page's 'the last stronghold of the Senussi in Libya'. The ruling reaches 1930, inside the next window (see problems).

patch_check: --check-patch p1920-p1929: 7 entries, 7 ok, 0 rejected. --trial: all 7 applied; the ruling settled 4,167 cell-years in 3 years; the p1930 end anchor changes 1,849 cells. Of these, 1,389 (Kufra), 14 (Vilnius) and 14 (Izmir) come from this patch; 252 Mozambique, 179 Rwanda/Burundi and 1 Swiss cell come from dossier edits or other windows' patches since the published compile. Rhodesia is unchanged at the end anchor; it changes only in 1923-1925.
problems: rulings/0 reaches 1930, into window p1930-p1939, on purpose: the British Africa 1930 keyframe would otherwise retake Kufra a year before the Italian seizure of 1931. p1930-p1939 should check that Kufra passes to Italian Libya in 1931-1932 (Senussi ledger 12: Jawf disc only, 236 cells, in 1931; the rest of the district at the 1932 dissolve) and that British Africa's 1932 keyframe does not take it back.

keyframe_overrides/1 and /2 change shapes valid 1924-1935, so they also act in 1930-1935 (window p1930-p1939); the effect is wanted. The 1936 shapes repeat the error: Cliopatria's Lithuania 1936 holds the same 14 Vilnius-disc cells and Poland 1936 lacks them, so the 1936 snap will hand Vilnius to Lithuania three years early. p1930-p1939 needs the same pair of overrides on kingdom-of-lithuania_1936 and second-polish-republic_1936 (source: Republic of Central Lithuania, 10 October 1939).

The window agent left about 550 Libyan cells as British Africa because 'pages silent', but the Second Italo-Senussi War page names Ajdabiya ('Jalu, Jaghbub, Awjila, and Ajdabiya') among the oases Idris was permitted to administer under al-Rajma. In the trial British Africa still wins 258 Ajdabiya and 118 Al Butnan cells in 1924 and 251 + 23 in 1926 by R1. The page does not date the Italian recovery of Ajdabiya, so this is not patchable from that page alone, but those cells were never British.

Pre-existing, not caused by the patch: from 1926 the British Africa 1926 keyframe drops 57 Rhodesian edge cells; 29 Zambian cells go to nobody and 28 Zimbabwe/Zambia cells go to estado-novo, the same as in the published draft. Edge noise for the colour/hierarchy pass.
